name: Vaccine Waning Models
title: Vaccine Waning Models
answer: Vaccine waning models estimate how protection from a vaccine declines over time, both against infection and against severe outcomes such as hospitalisation and death. They sit within epidemiology and population health, and they feed directly into decisions about booster timing, priority groups and outbreak forecasting. The models range from simple decay curves fitted to observed rates to multi parameter systems that separate the effect of waning from the effect of new variants and changing contact patterns. Their central output is usually a time varying estimate of vaccine effectiveness rather than a single fixed number.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Vaccine waning models estimate how protection from a vaccine declines over time, both against infection and against severe outcomes such as hospitalisation and death. They sit within epidemiology and population health, and they feed directly into decisions about booster timing, priority groups and outbreak forecasting. The models range from simple decay curves fitted to observed rates to multi parameter systems that separate the effect of waning from the effect of new variants and changing contact patterns. Their central output is usually a time varying estimate of vaccine effectiveness rather than a single fixed number.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on routine surveillance data, linked immunisation registers, hospital admission records and, where available, serological survey results. In many settings the computation happens in statistical environments such as R or Python, with Bayesian inference packages used to fit the models, and on shared research computing rather than specialised hardware. Data linkage and cleaning usually consume more effort than the modelling itself, because records must be matched across systems that were not designed to talk to each other. Where individual level data cannot be shared, aggregate counts by age band and week are used instead.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts typically compare vaccinated and unvaccinated groups over calendar time, adjusting for age, prior infection, variant period and time since vaccination. Test negative designs, in which the vaccination status of people who test positive is compared with that of people who test negative, are common because they reduce some forms of bias. Waning is then estimated as a change in effectiveness across intervals since the last dose, often with smoothing or random effects to avoid unstable week to week estimates. Sensitivity analyses test how much the conclusions move when assumptions about prior exposure, reporting delays or waning of immunity from infection are changed.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: These models inform public health policy, so their provenance matters as much as their output, and the underlying data are usually held under strict access agreements. Personal health data used in linkage are governed by national privacy law and by ethics approval, and published estimates are normally released as aggregates. Model code and assumptions should be documented so that other groups can reproduce the result, and uncertainty should be reported rather than hidden behind a single point estimate. Where a model is used to justify a change in vaccination policy, the reasoning and its limits belong in the public record.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward models that update as new data arrive, rather than being refitted months later, and toward combining waning estimates with genomic surveillance of circulating variants. There is growing interest in separating the effects of waning immunity, immune escape and changes in exposure, since these have different policy consequences. Wider use of linked national datasets and standardised reporting of time since vaccination would make estimates more comparable across countries. The main constraint is not modelling technique but the quality, timeliness and legal availability of the data that feed it.
